checks.reason: 雖宗族無能識者 says that no one in the clan recognized his worth, not that few knew him. 惟叔父耽幼而奇之 sets Dan apart as the only one who saw it while Yu was still young. 標秀 becomes outstanding talent, and 佐時之良器 becomes a fine instrument for serving the age, restoring 良 (fine). 皆 (all his brothers) and 單煢獨立 (utterly alone) are kept too. Uncle Dan is named in the Chinese, so no one is identified by inference.
checks.after: Orphaned young, with all his brothers also dying early, he stood utterly alone. None even in his clan recognized his worth; only his uncle Dan thought him extraordinary while he was still young, saying, "This child is not only an outstanding talent of our family but also a fine instrument for serving the age."

checks.reason: The proposal rightly corrects the first clause, 何事非君, to 'Whom may I not serve as ruler?'. But it renders 何使非民 as 'Whose people may I not serve?', which is a definite misreading. In Mencius (萬章下 and 公孫丑上), 使 is Yi Yin employing or commanding the people: Zhu Xi glosses it 所使者無非民, and Legge translates 'What people may I not command?'. Serving is the role of the first clause; the second is about directing the people. The amendment changes only that clause and keeps the rest of the proposal word for word, including 匏瓜 (bottle gourd), 聖賢 (sages and worthies) and 況吾曹乎 (how much more our sort).
checks.after: Yang Yu told his friend Cheng Pan, "Confucius welcomed Bi Xi's summons and likened himself to a bottle gourd; Yi Yin also said, 'Whom may I not serve as ruler? What people may I not command?' If even sages and worthies acted thus, how much more should we!

checks.reason: 知機其神 echoes the Yijing's 知幾其神乎 (to know the first signs of change is divine), and has nothing to do with 'Heaven calling'. The new text renders it as insight into the first signs of change, with 抑亦 as 'surely … also'. 追蹤伊、孔 becomes 'follow in the footsteps of Yi Yin and Confucius', and Cheng Pan's closing quotation mark is kept.
checks.after: You follow in the footsteps of Yi Yin and Confucius; surely your insight into the first signs of change is also extraordinary.”

checks.reason: 城池宮闔 covers city walls, moats, palaces and gates, and 'walls and towers' left out the moats and the palace gates. 皆裕之規模 says the plans were Yu's, which the new text makes explicit. 雅有巧思 (he had long had an ingenious mind) is restored, and 遷都和龍 is kept as the move of the capital to Helong. Huang (皝) stays the one who built.
checks.after: When the capital was moved to Helong, Yang Yu, who had long possessed an ingenious mind, drew up the plans for all the city walls, moats, palaces and gates that Murong Huang built.

checks.reason: 仕皝日近 means Yu's service under Huang was recent or short, not that he 'grew daily closer'. The new text fixes this and keeps the contrast with 寵秩在舊人之右 (his favor and rank above the old retainers). All the paired traits are kept: 謙恭 humble and respectful, 清儉 upright and frugal, 剛簡 firm and straightforward, 慈篤 compassionate and sincere. 曆居朝端 becomes successively holding leading posts, and the plain-clothed scholar simile is kept.
checks.after: Although Yang Yu had served Murong Huang for only a short time, his favor and rank surpassed those of the old retainers. By nature he was humble, respectful, upright and frugal, firm and straightforward, compassionate and sincere; although he successively held leading posts at court, he lived like a scholar in plain clothes.

checks.reason: The current text squeezes everything into 'buried exiles' and 'honored every gentleman'. It loses 經營 (making the arrangements), the separate 存恤孤遺 (care for the orphans and bereaved), the wording 無賢不肖 (worthy or unworthy alike), 傾身 (devoting himself) and 所在推仰 (esteemed wherever he went). The new text restores all of these. 'Who died' only spells out what 收葬 already implies.
checks.after: For displaced and isolated gentlemen who died, he invariably arranged their collection and burial, cared for the orphans and bereaved they left, and devoted himself to receiving gentlemen, worthy or unworthy alike; thus he was esteemed wherever he went.

additionalCorrections.before: East defeated Goguryeo, north destroyed Yuwen Gui—both he pre-planned their strategies; Huang greatly prized and employed him.
additionalCorrections.after: East defeated Goguryeo, north destroyed Yuwen Gui—in both he took part in the planning; Huang greatly prized and employed him.
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: In 皆豫其謀, 豫 stands for 與 and means to take part in. Yu took part in the planning of both campaigns. 'Pre-planned their strategies' misreads 豫 as 'beforehand'. The idiomatic field already says 'He helped plan' correctly, so only that clause in the literal field changes.
